findings.title: Compat alias `family` injected while backend still guards on ENABLED_FAMILIES
findings.why_it_matters: The comment says `family` is a temporary compat alias pending Step 11. But `ENABLED_FAMILIES` — a hardcoded Python set in config.py — continues to be the actual gating authority at four call sites (lines 1302, 2806, 2866, 3575, 3627). The new `prefix_catalog[*].authorable` field is the declared authority on the frontend but is completely ignored by the backend. This splits authorability truth across two authorities: a hardcoded config.py constant and the new registry schema. A future author adding a new prefix must update both independently, with no cross-check. The compat alias signals that Step 11 is planned but unscheduled; in the meantime the alias silently keeps stale gating alive rather than forcing the migration to resolve the split.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace all `ENABLED_FAMILIES` guard sites in service.py with a check against `action_spec.get('authorable', True)` derived from the normalized registry spec, then delete ENABLED_FAMILIES from config.py. Remove the `family` compatibility alias from `_normalize_template_action_spec` after all four guard sites are migrated. This aligns backend gating with the new schema authority.

findings.title: isTemplateActionAuthorable gate 4 re-checks identity already guaranteed by the catalog key
findings.why_it_matters: Gate 4 (lines 7013-7014) verifies that `prefixSpec.filename_prefix === prefix` and `prefixSpec.skin_family === skinFamily`. The value of `prefix` was derived from `spec.filename_prefix`, and `prefixSpec` was looked up by doing `prefix_catalog[prefix]`. If the catalog is internally consistent (enforced at load time by `_normalize_template_registry`), this check is permanently vacuous — the catalog lookup already proves the identity. When a future developer reads the function they will either infer the check is meaningful (and waste time understanding why) or correctly infer it's redundant but not remove it for fear of regression. The only case it could trigger is if the catalog JSON had a key/value mismatch, which is already caught server-side. The check adds two lines of parse-trim noise and a false signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the two identity re-check lines (7013-7014). The lookup `prefix_catalog[prefix]` guarantees `prefixSpec.filename_prefix === prefix` if the server-side normalizer is correct. Add a brief comment on the lookup line explaining the server guarantees this invariant.

findings.title: _resolve_preview_xp_fields helper called from exactly one site
findings.why_it_matters: _resolve_preview_xp_fields() is a 9-line helper extracted for a single call at line 985. The logic it encapsulates — fall back to l0_ref fields when preview_xp is absent — is simple enough that inlining it in _normalize_template_action_spec would reduce the cognitive hop without increasing the complexity of the caller. Right now a reader of _normalize_template_action_spec must navigate to the helper to understand the fallback contract. A docstring on the helper partially mitigates this but the extra level of indirection still exists for a single consumer.
findings.suggested_fix: Inline the two-branch fallback directly in _normalize_template_action_spec. If the fallback logic is expected to grow or be reused by additional callers in Step 11, keep the helper but note its future consumers explicitly in a comment.

findings.title: schema_version defaults to 2 silently for any malformed or v0 registry
findings.why_it_matters: The normalizer writes `schema_version = 2` when the field is absent from the JSON, meaning a v0/v1 registry that is missing the key is promoted to v2 silently rather than rejected. If such a registry passes normalization (it won't if mandatory fields are missing, but could if only schema_version is absent while all fields happen to be present), the caller cannot distinguish 'was already v2' from 'was promoted without validation'. A future schema v3 migration relying on `schema_version` to detect which registries need migration would skip any file that had the key silently injected. The guard should either assert the key is already present or raise with an explicit message for unexpected versions.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the block to raise ValueError if schema_version is present but is not 2, and accept absent schema_version as a v1-compat signal that triggers a deprecation warning rather than silent promotion. This preserves backward-compat for v1 files while making future migration logic reliable.
evidence: src/pipeline_v2/service.py:1079-1080 — `if 'schema_version' not in registry: registry['schema_version'] = 2`
config/template_registry.json:2 — current file already has schema_version 2, so the fallback never fires in production — but it will fire for any future consumer that omits the key

findings.title: prefix_catalog data duplicates template_sets action fields with drift-check at load time only
findings.why_it_matters: The prefix_catalog and template_sets.*.actions share filename_prefix, skin_family, preview_xp, preview_xp_sha256, l0_ref, l0_ref_sha256 for the same physical prefixes. For example, `player` appears in prefix_catalog with all six fields, and identically in player_native_idle_only.actions.idle and player_native_full.actions.idle. The normalizer validates that these match at load time (lines 1070-1077), which is good. But the data is stored redundantly in the JSON file itself, so any edit in one place requires a matching edit in at least two others (up to N template_sets times M actions per prefix). The normalizer's drift-check will catch the mismatch at runtime, not at authoring time, making the JSON brittle for hand-edits. The JSON grew from 79 to 265 lines largely because of this duplication. A cleaner design would store the canonical per-prefix metadata only in prefix_catalog and have template_sets.actions reference just the template_set_key and action_key, deriving fields at load time.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider storing per-action geometry (xp_dims, angles, frames, etc.) only in template_sets.actions and per-prefix identity fields (filename_prefix, skin_family, preview_xp, l0_ref + hashes) only in prefix_catalog. The normalizer already joins them at load time — use that join to populate action specs from the catalog rather than storing both and drift-checking. This would cut the JSON size and eliminate duplicate maintenance.

findings.title: _load_reference_l0 and _load_reference_l1 duplicate registry-scan loop
findings.why_it_matters: Both _load_reference_l0 (lines 1110-1118) and _load_reference_l1 (lines 1178-1186) contain an identical nested loop: iterate all template_sets, iterate all actions, find the first action whose `family` matches the argument, extract l0_ref_path. The loops are copied verbatim. With the prefix_catalog now available in the normalized registry, the lookup could be a direct dict access (`prefix_catalog[family].l0_ref`) instead of an O(sets*actions) scan. The duplication means any future change to how the ref path is located must be applied in both functions.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a private `_get_l0_ref_path(family: str) -> str | None` that does a single `prefix_catalog[family]['l0_ref']` lookup on the normalized registry. Both _load_reference_l0 and _load_reference_l1 call this helper instead of duplicating the nested loop.
evidence: src/pipeline_v2/service.py:1110-1118 — nested for-loop in _load_reference_l0 scanning for matching family
src/pipeline_v2/service.py:1178-1186 — identical nested for-loop in _load_reference_l1
config/template_registry.json:45-152 — prefix_catalog now provides a direct O(1) lookup path by prefix

findings.title: test_template_registry_actions_are_normalized hardcodes skin_family == 'human'
findings.why_it_matters: The original diff snapshot of the test file (line 576 in the diff) asserted `action['skin_family'] == 'human'` unconditionally. The committed version softened this to `action['skin_family'] in registry['skin_family_scope']` which is reasonable. However the API-level test (test_templates_api_exposes_normalized_contract) asserts `human_scope['mounted_prefixes'] == ['wolfie', 'wolack']` as an exact list equality. This encodes current data fixture values as a contract assertion. When a new mounted prefix is added to the human scope, this test will fail not because something broke but because the data changed — a false alarm that wastes the next developer's time before they understand it's a data assertion, not a behavioral one.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace exact list equality for mounted_prefixes with a subset/superset check or a `len >= 2` check alongside an `in` check for the specific prefix names being tested. Alternatively, add a comment making clear the test is a data-contract assertion that must be updated when prefixes are added.
evidence: tests/test_template_registry_schema.py:91 — `assert human_scope['mounted_prefixes'] == ['wolfie', 'wolack']` (exact list equality on data)
tests/test_template_registry_schema.py:56-57 — same pattern for mounted_scope_is_explicit test

residual_risks: ENABLED_FAMILIES in config.py and the new prefix_catalog.authorable field are split authorities for the same gating decision. Until Step 11 is completed, adding a new authorable prefix requires updating both. If a developer updates only the registry JSON, the backend will still reject the new prefix.

The schema_version silent-upgrade path means a corrupted or partial registry file could be promoted to v2 without error if it happens to include all required fields but lacks the schema_version key. There is no lower-bound version enforcement.
The prefix_catalog drift-check runs only at server startup (load_template_registry is cached). If the JSON file is edited and the server is not restarted, the drift check does not re-run.

The frontend isTemplateActionAuthorable reads state.templateRegistry via a module-level closure on `state`. This is not a pure function — tests that want to exercise it with synthetic registry data must mutate global state, which is fragile.
testing_gaps: No test exercises the backend ENABLED_FAMILIES guard paths with a prefix that is `authorable: false` in the new schema. The split authority means the backend guard could be removed accidentally without any test catching it.
No test for _load_reference_l0 or _load_reference_l1 verifying that the family-scan loop returns None for an unknown family — only the load-time L0 status tracking is tested indirectly.
No test covers isTemplateActionAuthorable in isolation in JS. The function is only exercised via the full UI rendering path.
